source_text: At hunc fides catholica in utroque contrivit; malum scilicet in carne non esse naturaliter, atque ob hoc Christo nec aliquid defuisse humanitatis, nec quidquam iniquitatis adfuisse pronuntians. Clamat ergo dispensationis suae conscius: Ecce venit princeps huius mundi, et invenit in me nihil [n119] ; nihil profecto quod possit arguere, quia non poterat infamare naturam, cuius ad peccata non inflexerat voluntatem.
pass_a_gloss: But the catholic faith crushed him in both; pronouncing namely that evil is not in the flesh naturally, and on account of this that nothing of humanity was lacking to Christ, nor was anything of iniquity present. He therefore, conscious of his dispensation, cries: Behold, the prince of this world is coming, and he finds nothing in me; nothing indeed that he can accuse, because he could not infame a nature whose will he had not bent toward sins.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: But the catholic faith crushed him on both points. It declares that evil does not exist naturally in flesh and that therefore Christ lacked nothing human and possessed nothing unjust. Conscious of his own saving work, he cries: “See, the ruler of this world is coming, and he finds nothing in me” (John 14:30). Certainly nothing he could accuse: he could not defame a nature whose will he had not bent toward sins.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
